qa.answer: It reads the documents a filter matches from a MongoDB collection and stores them as minified relaxed Extended JSON, together with their field names and their count.
qa.question: What does the ExportMongoDbQuery plugin do?

qa.answer: Collection is required; CommandText, CommandFile, and Base64 carry the filter; Projection, Sort, Limit, and Skip shape the result; the connection comes from Credentials or ConnectionString, and Database selects the database. Outputs are Columns, DocumentCount, and Result.

qa.answer: It runs as an Action task step with the database icon and the ActionRuleModel, usually before steps that iterate or assert on the exported documents.
qa.question: How does ExportMongoDbQuery fit into an automation workflow?

qa.answer: Project only the fields a flow needs, always pair Skip with a Sort, limit large collections, and read the decoded ExportMongoDbQuery:Result instead of re-querying.
qa.question: What are best practices for using ExportMongoDbQuery?

qa.answer: Use $type “Action” with pluginName “ExportMongoDbQuery” and pass inputs in the argument, such as {{$ --Credentials:mongo-production --Collection:orders --CommandText:{"status":"open"}}}.

qa.answer: A malformed filter, an unresolved database, an invalid Base64 payload, or a missing CommandFile fails the step, while a filter that matches nothing stores an empty array with a DocumentCount of 0.

Are macros resolved inside a Base64-encoded CommandText?
qa.answer: Yes. With the Base64 switch set, the action decodes CommandText and then resolves its macros, because the engine cannot see macros while the value is encoded. CommandFile content keeps its macros as written.

description: ### Purpose
Reads the documents of a MongoDB collection into an automation.
The filter, the projection, and the sort travel as BSON, so no value is ever composed into a query.
Stores the documents as relaxed Extended JSON, which keeps the BSON types that plain JSON cannot express.
### Key Features and Functionality
| Feature                    | Description                                                                                                                                  |
| Filter as data             | Reads the filter from CommandText, CommandFile, or Base64-encoded text and binds it as BSON.                                                 |
| Match-all default          | An omitted filter matches every document, so a step can export a whole collection.                                                           |
| Result shaping             | Applies Projection, Sort, Limit, and Skip only when the step sets them, so unset options keep the server default.                             |
| Field names                | Reports the union of the top-level field names, in first-seen order, because documents are schemaless.                                        |
| Extended JSON              | Serializes object identifiers, dates, and decimals through their Extended JSON type form, so a later step can address them.                   |
| Session and entity outputs | Stores outputs as Base64 session parameters named `ExportMongoDbQuery:<Name>` and returns them in the response entity unless `NoEntity` is set. |
### Usages in RPA
| Use Case             | Description                                                                              |
| Work queue intake    | Read the pending documents a bot must process, sorted by priority and limited per run.   |
| Reporting extract    | Export the documents of a date range, projected to the fields a report needs.            |
| Reference lookup     | Read the configuration documents a later step binds into its own arguments.               |
### Usages in Automation Testing
| Use Case          | Description                                                                         |
| Data-driven tests | Read the test cases of a collection and iterate the exported documents.             |
| Result assertion  | Read the documents a flow wrote and compare them with the expected content.         |
| State inspection  | Read one document by its identifier to confirm a prior step changed it as expected.  |
### Notes
CommandText wins over CommandFile, and the Base64 switch decodes only CommandText.
A limit of 0 and a skip of 0 mean the option is not set, which matches the server default.
Outputs are plain text in the response entity and Base64-encoded in the session parameters.
Stores the union of the top-level field names of the exported documents, as a JSON array.
Reports the field names in the order they were first seen, which follows the projection order.
Returned as plain text in the response entity for direct data transfer.

edge_cases: Result larger than the session parameter a later step expects
annotations.expected_result: The step stores the matching documents in `ExportMongoDbQuery:Result`, their field names in `ExportMongoDbQuery:Columns`, and their count in `ExportMongoDbQuery:DocumentCount`.
annotations.notes: The filter binds as BSON, so its values never become part of a composed query. An empty result is reported as an empty array with a count of 0.

description: ### Read the documents a filter matches
The argument names the collection and passes the filter as a JSON object.
The step stores the documents as relaxed Extended JSON.

edge_cases: Projection excludes every field of interest
Skip without a sort returns unstable pages
Limit smaller than the number of matching documents
annotations.expected_result: The step stores at most 100 projected documents, ordered by the newest first, in `ExportMongoDbQuery:Result`.
annotations.notes: Projection, Sort, Limit, and Skip apply only when set, so an unset option keeps the server default. Page with a sort, so the pages stay stable between runs.

description: ### Export a projected, sorted page
The argument shapes the result with a projection, a sort, a limit, and a skip.
The projection keeps the exported documents small, which matters for a session parameter.

edge_cases: Filter contains ` --` or `}}`, which end an inline argument
annotations.expected_result: The step decodes the filter and stores the matching documents in `ExportMongoDbQuery:Result`.
annotations.notes: Encode a filter that carries inline-argument terminators, or pass it through CommandFile instead. Invalid Base64 fails the step before any query runs.

description: ### Export with a Base64-encoded filter
The `Base64` switch marks CommandText as UTF-8 Base64, so a filter with special sequences survives the inline argument.
The decoded filter is `{"name":{"$regex":"^A"}}`.

edge_cases: CommandFile points to a missing file
File holds a JSON array instead of an object
annotations.expected_result: The step reads the filter from the file and stores the matching documents in `ExportMongoDbQuery:Result`.
annotations.notes: CommandText wins over CommandFile, and file content is always read as plain text, so the Base64 switch never applies to it.

description: ### Export with a filter from a file
The argument reads the filter from a UTF-8 file, which suits a long or reused filter.
NoEntity keeps the outputs in session parameters only.

edge_cases: Connection URI names an unreachable host
Database argument names a database the login cannot read
Credentials parameter set together with ConnectionString
annotations.expected_result: The step exports up to 50 closed orders of archive.orders into `ExportMongoDbQuery:Documents` and reports their number in `ExportMongoDbQuery:Count`.
annotations.notes: ConnectionString applies only when Credentials is not set. The Database argument replaces the database the URI carries, so one stored URI serves several databases.

description: ### Export documents with a connection URI
The argument passes a complete MongoDB connection URI instead of a stored credentials record, which suits a local or containerized deployment.
The URI names the shop database, and the Database argument selects archive instead, so the step reads `archive.orders`.

edge_cases: Base64 switch is absent, so the macro inside the encoded text stays hidden and is not resolved
Value is passed plain, so the engine resolves its macros before the plugin runs
The payload comes from CommandFile, so its macros are kept as written
annotations.expected_result: The step stores the orders created today in `ExportMongoDbQuery:Result`.
annotations.notes: The engine resolves the macros of a rule before the plugin runs, when the Base64 value still hides them, so the plugin resolves the macros of the decoded payload itself. Encoding also keeps the closing braces of the JSON from ending the inline argument value.

description: ### Export today's orders with a Base64 filter that holds a macro
The argument binds the `mongo-production` credentials, a Base64 CommandText, and the Base64 switch at runtime.
The decoded payload is `{"createdOn":{"$gte":"{{$New-Date --Format:yyyy-MM-dd}}"}}`; the New-Date macro is resolved after decoding, so the server receives the current date.

The session value is Base64-encoded, so decode it before comparing or displaying it.

description: Reads CommandText as UTF-8 Base64 and decodes it before use.
After decoding, the macros in the decoded value are resolved, because the engine resolves the macros of a rule before the plugin runs and cannot see them while the value is encoded.
Use it for a payload that contains ` --` or `}}`, which end an inline argument value.
Invalid Base64 fails the step, so an encoded payload never reaches the server as text.
parameters.name: Base64

description: Names the collection the step operates on, such as `orders` or `shop.orders`.
A name qualified as `database.collection` selects its own database and overrides the Database parameter.
The name is split on its first dot only, so `shop.price.history` addresses the collection `price.history`.
parameters.name: Collection

description: Reads the payload from a UTF-8 file, such as `C:\flows\filter.json`.
Applies only when CommandText is not set, so an inline payload always takes priority.
The Base64 switch never applies here; file content is always read as plain text.
parameters.name: CommandFile

description: Supplies the query filter as a JSON object, such as `{"status":"open"}`.
An omitted filter matches every document, so the step exports the whole collection.
Both Extended JSON forms are accepted, so `{"_id":{"$oid":"..."}}` addresses an object identifier.
parameters.name: CommandText

description: Sets the time budget, in seconds, for connecting, selecting a server, and running the operation.
The value 0 means no operation timeout, so the step waits until the server answers.
Raise it for a long aggregation and lower it for a health check that must fail fast.
parameters.name: CommandTimeout

description: Supplies a full MongoDB connection URI, such as `mongodb://localhost:27017/shop`.
Applies only when Credentials is not set, so a stored credentials reference always takes priority.
Every connection setting, such as the host, the login, the replica set, and the TLS mode, is written into the URI itself.
parameters.name: ConnectionString

description: Names a stored MongoDB credentials record by name or id, such as `mongo-production`, so secrets stay out of the rule.
The record carries the host, port, login, replica set, and TLS settings, so the step never repeats them.
A value that carries a URI scheme, such as `mongodb://`, is used as a raw connection URI instead, and any other value that matches no record fails the step.
parameters.name: Credentials

description: Names the database the step operates on, such as `shop`.
Selects the database next to the collection, and replaces the database the credentials record or the connection URI carries.
A collection named as `database.collection` overrides this parameter in turn.
parameters.name: Database

description: Limits the number of exported documents, such as `100`.
The value 0 means no limit, so the step exports every matching document.
parameters.name: Limit

description: Omits the response entity, so the step reports its outputs only as session parameters.
Use it when a later step reads the outputs by name and no data transfer is needed.
parameters.name: NoEntity

description: Selects the fields the server returns, as a JSON object such as `{"name":1,"_id":0}`.
An omitted projection returns the whole document.
parameters.name: Projection

description: Skips the first documents of the result, such as `50` for the second page of fifty.
The value 0 means no skip, and a skip without a sort has no stable meaning.
parameters.name: Skip

description: Orders the documents before the limit and the skip apply, as a JSON object such as `{"createdAt":-1}`.
An omitted sort leaves the order to the server, which is not stable across runs.
parameters.name: Sort
